title: Sanford Health Return to Running Guidelines (post-surgical, tendon and soft-tissue interval running programs)
population: Patients returning to running after lower-extremity injury or surgery; no outcome data
findings: Ready-to-run test: walk 30 min (about 3.0-3.5 mph), 25+ single-leg heel raises, step-ups, double-leg jumps and single-leg hops at 180 bpm, single-leg squats; all must be pain-free.

Post-surgical programme: run every other day at conversation pace (50-60% of max HR); each level done 3 times pain-free; Level 1 run 3 / walk 4 x3, L2 4/3 x3, L3 6/3 x3, L4 8-10 min or 1 mile / walk 2 x2.

Tendon and soft-tissue programme (tendinopathies and chronic strains): each level twice, 2-3 days between runs (72 h for tendon collagen net synthesis); L1 run 5 min continuous, L2 10, L3 15, L4 20, L5 25, L6 30 min, plus 30-60+ min walk or cross-training on non-running days.

Continue if gait is normal, pain is 5/10 or less and improves during the run, pain returns to baseline within 24 h, and the trend does not worsen week to week. Acute sprains and strains may need a more gradual walk/run approach; patients who kept running through the injury may start further along.
limitations: Clinical convention (D); the page calls it 'evidence-based' but cites no study for the levels; no outcome data; written for rehabilitation, not for novices; year is from the document code '1/24' and file creation date (Jan 2024).
implications: For a rehabilitating runner the soft-tissue floor is 5-10 min of continuous running, reaching 20 min continuous at the 7th run when each level is done twice; 3 x 20 is too high a floor for that group.
Supports 2-3 days between runs while a tendon or soft-tissue injury is recent, which fits 2-3 runs per week for a flagged runner; applying this to a generic injury flag is an extrapolation.
